The third plane is labeled III. It's vertical, intersects the first plane along a horizontal line, and intersects the second plane along a vertical line.

The three planes have no point in common: No solutions. An inconsistent system.
Three planes labeled I, II, and III, respectively are shown in three different arrangements.
In the first arrangement, all three planes are vertical. Each pair of planes intersects along a different vertical line, so the three planes don't have a common intersection.
In the second arrangement, the three planes are all horizontal. Plane I is above plane II which is above plane III. None of the planes intersect.

In the third arrangement, plane I is vertical, and planes II and III are horizontal with plane II above plane III. Planes I and II intersect along a horizontal line, and planes I and III intersect along a different horizontal line, so the three planes don't have a common intersection.
